requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) runs a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 was assigned 10.50.50.254/24 and a Kea DHCPv4 shared-network 'LAN' (subnet 10.50.50.0/24, range .100-.200, subnet-id 1, authoritative) was configured, committed, and saved. `listen-interface eth1` scopes the server so it only binds 10.50.50.254:67, not the egress NIC. Post-config `ss -ulnp` confirms kea-dhcp4 listening only on 10.50.50.254:67, and systemctl shows isc-kea-dhcp4-server active.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain their address on the private network from node1 via DHCP rather than static assignment
requirements.summary: Both node2 and node3's enp8s0 NM profiles have ipv4.method=auto (dynamic). After bringing the connections up, node2 leased 10.50.50.100 and node3 leased 10.50.50.101, both with 'dynamic' flag shown in `ip addr`. node1's Kea lease CSV independently records both leases keyed to node2/node3 hostnames, corroborating node1 as the DHCP source.

requirements.requirement: Connectivity is functional on the DHCP-served private network
requirements.summary: node2 successfully pinged node1 (10.50.50.254) and node3 (10.50.50.101) over enp8s0 both before and after the restart cycle, with 0% packet loss in both runs.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: For each node: a pre-restart boot_id and health check was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node was unreachable during the transition, a new boot_id was observed confirming the restart, and recovered state was verified (node1: kea service active, eth1 address intact, lease CSV persisted with both prior leases; node2/node3: DHCP re-acquired same leased addresses via ipv4.method=auto). The fixed after-executor snapshot boot identities (05537890.../84ce8bed.../c548c1e3...) match the executor's own final observations, cross-confirming the transitions were real.

overall_summary: node1 was configured as an authoritative Kea DHCP server scoped to the private eth1 network (10.50.50.0/24, pool .100-.200), and node2/node3 were confirmed to already use dynamic (ipv4.method=auto) addressing on their matching enp8s0 NICs; both leased addresses from node1 as shown in node1's lease table and via successful bidirectional pings. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed and directly observed for all three nodes, with distinct pre/post boot identities, a bounded unreachable window during each reboot, and recovered DHCP service/lease/connectivity state afterward, corroborated by the fixed after-executor snapshot boot identities.
limitations: Lease persistence evidence for node1 across its own reboot relies on the same /config/dhcp/dhcp4-leases.csv file rather than a fresh client-initiated DHCPDISCOVER/OFFER exchange post-reboot, so it demonstrates data persistence but not a live re-lease event on node1 itself.

The cluster only has three nodes and no explicit 'cluster state' concept beyond the three managed nodes, so cluster-state recovery is inferred from per-node service and connectivity checks rather than a dedicated cluster-level health check.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: interface addressing and Kea DHCP configuration on node1 (necessary for the task), bringing up the enp8s0 connections on node2/node3 (necessary prerequisite since they were down at start), and the mandated one-at-a-time reboot protocol on all three nodes (independent requirement, executed safely and sequentially). Several early attempts to configure DHCP on node1 failed at commit time (e.g. cmd-3996da2eecd04bb5 with invalid subnet-parameters/default-router paths, cmd-593491dc18144016 with an invalid '?' path) — these are read/probe-oriented syntax discovery attempts inside a VyOS configure session that failed before commit, so no persisted state was mutated; they represent normal iterative discovery of the correct Kea CLI syntax rather than unnecessary or residue-producing mutations. No abandoned files, conflicting/failed services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state are visible in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare (failed-services empty on all nodes both before and after; package-health managers unchanged). Reboot-induced /tmp systemd-private directories are expected reboot artifacts, not executor residue.
